DRC General Strike Ends as Mining and Transport Sectors Resume Operations

A nationwide general strike that disrupted key industries across the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has ended after a four-day standstill, with major companies, including Katanga Mining Ltd, resuming normal operations. The strike, organized by a coalition of labor unions, effectively halted mining, transportation, and retail activities, causing significant delays at ports and a slowdown in mineral exports.

The work stoppage was sparked by demands for increased wages and improved working conditions in the public and private sectors. According to the Congolese Chamber of Commerce, the mining sector alone lost an estimated $38 million per day in output during the strike. “This has been one of the most coordinated industrial actions in recent Congolese history,” said Lucien Mwamba, an analyst at Kinshasa-based consultancy AfriLogic. “The impact on copper and cobalt exports was immediate, with shipments from key sites, including those operated by Katanga Mining Ltd, temporarily suspended.”

Negotiations between union leaders and government officials concluded late Monday, with an agreement to review wage structures and initiate a joint commission on labor standards. “We are satisfied with the government’s commitment to address our concerns,” stated Jean-Marc Ilunga, spokesperson for the Congolese Trade Union Federation. “Our members have returned to work, but we expect swift action on the promises made.”

Katanga Mining Ltd confirmed all operations had resumed as of Tuesday morning. Logistics firm TransAfrica Freight also reported that freight movements at Matadi port were back to normal levels. Investors are now watching closely for longer-term impacts on the DRC’s crucial mining sector and broader economic stability.
